title: A Systematic Analysis of a Small Optimal Subspace for Physics-Informed Neural Networks: $n$-DAS $\subset \mathbb{R}^p$
abstract: arXiv:2611.23773v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The search for a low-dimensional subspace that governs neural network training has been a persistent goal in optimization. Yet subspaces defined by Hessian eigenvalue magnitude, such as the dominant/bulk decomposition underlying Dom-SGD and Bulk-SGD, have repeatedly failed to capture where optimization takes place, and adaptive Krylov-based alternatives built on energy-fraction thresholds show promise but still struggle at lower eigenmodes. We argue this failure is structural: the directions of highest curvature are not, in general, the directions along which training moves. We introduce the dominant aligned subspace (DAS), constructed from a full eigendecomposition of the Hessian but selected by gradient alignment rather than eigenvalue magnitude, as a tool for understanding optimization dynamics and a foundation for designing methods that exploit them. tldr: 该论文提出“主导对齐子空间”（DAS），通过梯度对齐而非Hessian特征值大小来选择低维优化子空间，论证了最高曲率方向并非训练实际移动的方向，并以物理信息神经网络为对象对该结构进行了系统分析。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Dominant Aligned Subspace (DAS), selected by gradient alignment rather than Hessian eigenvalue magnitude, arguing that the directions of highest curvature are generally not those along which training moves, and systematically analyzes this small optimal subspace for physics-informed neural networks.
